model: Launch white WUP-001 Basic, original WUP-010 GamePad

sources.scope: Original console and GamePad component identification; front/rear layout and control types.
Official white front image used for image-fit coordinates, camera/IR cover, analog cap proportions and legends.
Correct side of volume, headphone and charging connector; original stylus holder and rear SYNC control. Rear-view X is opposite the front convention.
Capsule eject key and front control/compartment layout; front cover is open in the reference.
Rear USB position, three-by-seven exhaust field and remaining connector ordering.
WUP-002 150 x 70 x 49 mm; WUP-011 100 x 35 x 28 mm; WUP-015 height5.4 x width8.4 x length97.9 mm. Optional stands listed nearby are not added to the Basic kit.
Rear GamePad SYNC control is operated with the supplied stylus.
Original GamePad top/back/bottom diagrams distinguish the top TV-control infrared window from the front sensor bar and locate charging terminals on the bottom edge beside the accessory connector.

front_image_fit.rule: local x=(pixel x-587.5)*255.4/1081; local y=(480-pixel y)*133.4/570. Coordinates rounded for the model; image projection and edge selection are not manufacturing tolerances.
front_image_fit.geometry_note: These are image fits. The dimensions above are not directly published Nintendo mechanical measurements.

console_image_fit.basis: Official image fits. The main published plastic envelope remains 172 x 268.5 x 46 mm.

rear_and_accessory_changes.styling_state: Stylus remains a separate accessory, so its reconstructed holder is empty. HOME and battery indicator surfaces use the unlit appearance shown by the reference image.
rear_and_accessory_changes.adapter_numbering: Existing parameterized power-brick parts are rebuilt with the same PartIDs and registration order; cables begin at the revised strain-relief positions.
rear_and_accessory_changes.edge_features_basis: The manual confirms face and relative layout. Local dimensions are diagram/image fits; contact thickness and window shell profile are reconstructed.

limitations: No physical hardware scan or factory molding drawings were obtained.
Image-calibrated positions, cap/rim shapes, front-cover size, local wall thicknesses, port depth and optical-window geometry remain estimates.
The public adapter sizes are applied to the enclosure; cable/strain-relief projections are separate and the manufacturer's precise exclusion convention is not independently measured.
Button PCB outlines, case-post notches, fan/duct alignment, audio leads and the stylus guide are reconstructed internal accommodations, not factory PCB or airflow geometry.
Rear crossbar, shoulder surfaces, battery-cover proportions and fine molding transitions remain inherited approximations; the changed controls and ports do not constitute a scan-derived shell.
The rear SYNC cap is modeled; its unmeasured underlying switch package is not reproduced.
Photographs show an inserted stylus and open console front cover, while the study displays the stylus separately and normally closes that cover.
Reference images and manual pages remain local and are not redistributed.
